note: This matches every order in your POS export to NPMCM's SOA data by EXACT J&T TRACKING NUMBER - no name guessing. Column E pulls NPMCM's own status for that tracking number (or "Not yet in NPMCM" if it hasn't appeared in any of your uploaded SOAs). Column G tells you what to do about each row. The two things that matter most: (1) any row marked with a red flag below means your POS confirms the parcel was RETURNED but NPMCM still charged you COD for it as if delivered - that money should be credited back to you; (2) rows marked with an orange flag are parcels your POS confirms were DELIVERED to the customer but NPMCM has not yet shown as paid in any SOA you've uploaded - some of these are simply too recent (shipped after Jun 29, your latest uploaded SOA) and will show up once you upload the next batch; others may need you to follow up with NPMCM directly. Note: because many of your customers order more than once, the same name can legitimately appear several times here - that is expected and is why matching is done by tracking number, not name. Column H flags which POS file each row came from: "orders (4).xlsx" was a Delivered-only export from your POS, so it is excluded from the EXACT RTS RATE calculation below (mixing it in would make your RTS rate look artificially lower than it really is) but is still counted everywhere else. Column I flags "Y" for orders with Day Created on/before Apr 10, 2026 - per your own account, those were processed by hand via sheets/reports and can have the wrong POS Status (Delivered tagged when it wasn't, Returned tagged when it was actually delivered, duplicate tracking numbers under two order IDs). Treat column G's flag as a lead to verify, not a proven fact, for any row where column I = "Y".
